title: Run LoadFamily, Export, RequestViewChange and EditScope.Commit between WithTransaction blocks, not inside them
task: Load a family (or export a view, switch the active view, commit a StairsEditScope) in the same run as a write: these Revit calls transact themselves and require the target document NOT to be modifiable, so call them at top level between Connector.WithTransaction blocks. Inside a block they fail with script-target-must-not-be-modifiable. Their commit joins the run's group: a later throw still rolls it back.

pitfalls.symptom: `script-target-must-not-be-modifiable` from Document.LoadFamily, Document.Export, UIDocument.RequestViewChange or EditScope.Commit; Revit says the document must not be modifiable.
pitfalls.cause: The call was made inside a Connector.WithTransaction block, where the target is modifiable; these APIs open their own transaction.
pitfalls.fix: Move the call to top level, between blocks: block for writes, then the call, then another block.

pitfalls.symptom: A family loaded at top level is missing afterwards although LoadFamily returned it.
pitfalls.cause: The load's own commit is part of the run's transaction group; an uncaught throw anywhere later in the same run rolls the whole group back, load included. A run that succeeds keeps it.
pitfalls.fix: Keep the run free of uncaught throws after the load (catch and report instead), or reload in a later run; confirm with a Family collector.

pitfalls.symptom: NullReferenceException on UIDocument.RequestViewChange when routed at a created or background document.
pitfalls.cause: UIDocument is null there: Revit has no UI document for a headless document.
pitfalls.fix: Route the run at the active document (omit document_id) for view changes.
